notes:
Summary: Large regional bank evaluating Redwood Private (VPC) for customer-facing support agent + internal doc search. Primary ask = robust audit logging + SIEM-forwarding and KMS BYOK. High sensitivity on PII residency; legal requires EU residency for some datasets and 7-year audit logs for financial transactions.

Security review status: security questionnaire returned 2026-02-25 (see Drive). Initial architecture review 2026-03-02 with infra/security (FF id ff_2026-03-02_avt_arch_review). Key asks from security team: SIEM export (Splunk, QRadar, Datadog), well-defined JSON log schema (also accept CEF for legacy pipelines), retention policy mapping, access logs for model calls, and KMS key usage audit.

SIEM export details requested (customer specs):
- Primary transport: HTTPS (Splunk HEC) with mTLS; syslog over TLS as fallback.
- Formats: application JSON events (preferred) and CEF for SOC consumption.
- Required fields: timestamp (ISO8601, ns), request_id, client_ip (anonymized when PII), user_id (pseudonymized), route/model_id, model_version, token_counts{prompt,completion,total}, latency_ms, response_status, error_code, kv_cache_hit(true/false), crypto_key_id (for KMS ops), tenant_id, data_residency_flag, sampling_indicator.
- Enrichment: geo.country, infra.region, agent_version.

Retention & tiers:
- Audit-grade logs: 7 years (financial regs). Immutable (WORM) option needed for archive.
- Operational debug logs: 90 days raw, 13 months aggregate metrics.
- Access logs for model inference and KMS usage: retain 3 years online, archive to customer S3 for rest.

Access log specifics:
- Capture full request path (no raw prompt text stored by default for PII-sensitive routes) unless customer opts in; approach: store prompt hash + metadata + sampled plaintext for QA.
- Authentication metadata: SSO subject, API key id, IP, session id.
- Admin actions: config changes, model rollouts, key rotations must log user, timestamp, diff, and approval ticket id.

KMS integration notes:
- Customer requires BYOK using AWS KMS/CloudHSM (also open to Azure KeyVault).
- Redwood must emit key use audit events: key_create, key_rotate, key_decrypt_request, key_decrypt_success/fail with crypto_key_id and wrapping key fingerprint.
- Policy ask: ensure Redwood supports key rotation without data loss; confirm envelope encryption flows and zero-access guarantee for root keys.

POC scope discussed: deploy Private VPC in us-east-1, ingest logs into Aventine Splunk HEC endpoint, validate syslog fallback, run 2-week load with 100rps, verify retention/archival to their S3, and demonstrate KMS BYOK sign/unwrap events.

Quotes / customer soundbites: "We need machine-readable logs our SOC can alert on — and guarantees we can hand them off for compliance audits." Security lead: "No raw prompts to long-term logs unless approved and redacted."

Risks / red flags: legal still negotiating EU data residency carve-outs for cross-border fallbacks. SE noted potential perf impact if synchronous HEC forwarding required per request.

Docs shared: security questionnaire, proposed SIEM schema v0.1 (attached), pricing deck, example Splunk HEC ingestion playbook.

Short-term asks: finish SIEM schema v0.2 with field types + example events; produce KMS integration design doc; schedule POC kickoff week of 2026-03-22.
